answers.value: Statement I true, Statement II false
answers.reasoning: Statement I: \(3N\) is a multiple of 3, so \(3N+2\) leaves remainder 2. True. Statement II: N leaves remainder 3 on division by 5, so it ends in 3 or 8; N is even, so it ends in 8 (e.g. 8, 18, 28). Dividing by 10 leaves remainder 8, not 4. False.

I: exterior angles of a triangle add to \(360^\circ\), double the interior sum \(180^\circ\). True. II: interior sum \(= 2 \times 360^\circ = 720^\circ\), so \((n-2) \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ\) gives \(n = 6\), a hexagon. True. III: interior angles are \(30^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ\), so exterior angles are \(150^\circ, 120^\circ, 90^\circ\), in the ratio \(5 : 4 : 3\), not \(3 : 2 : 1\). False.
The work is \(7 \times 16 = 112\) man-days, so double the work is 224 man-days. To finish it in 8 days needs \(224 \div 8 = 28\) men.
Total marbles \(= 6 + 5 + 4 + 5 = 20\), of which 6 are red. Probability \(= \frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}\).
The primes from 1 to 16 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13: six of them. Probability \(= \frac{6}{16} = \frac{3}{8}\).

Cost \(= 160 \times 50 = ₹8000\). 70% of 160 kg is 112 kg sold at ₹70, giving ₹7840; the other 48 kg at ₹35 gives ₹1680. Selling price \(= ₹9520\), gain \(= ₹1520\), and \(\frac{1520}{8000} \times 100 = 19\%\).
Multiply the ratio by 18: \(a : b : c = 6 : 3 : 2\). Then \(\frac{a^2+b^2}{b^2-c^2} = \frac{36+9}{9-4} = \frac{45}{5} = 9\).
Selling price \(= 1500 \times 0.95 = ₹1425\). This is 125% of the cost, so cost \(= 1425 \div 1.25 = ₹1140\).
The food is \(200 \times 42 = 8400\) person-days. With 240 persons it lasts \(8400 \div 240 = 35\) days.
For a fixed distance, a higher speed means less time, and speed \(\times\) time stays constant. So speed and time vary inversely. The other pairs increase together (direct variation).
LCM of 6, 5, 7, 10 and 12 is 420, so the bells toll together every 420 seconds. One hour is 3600 seconds, and \(3600 \div 420 = 8.57\), so they toll together 8 times after the start.
Lateral surface area \(= 4a^2 = 256\), so \(a^2 = 64\) and \(a = 8\) m. Volume \(= 8^3 = 512 \text{ m}^3\).

AD is parallel to BC, so \(\angle ACB = \angle DAC = 45^\circ\) (alternate angles). \(\angle BOC = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ\). In triangle BOC, \(\angle OBC = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 45^\circ = 65^\circ\), and this is \(\angle DBC\).
Target: \(3ac - 3bc + 3c^2 - 2ac - 2bc + 2c^2 = ac - 5bc + 5c^2\). Given: \(-4ac - 8bc + 4c^2\). Subtract: \((ac - 5bc + 5c^2) - (-4ac - 8bc + 4c^2) = 5ac + 3bc + c^2\).
Wrong total \(= 30 \times 150 = 4500\) cm. The correct total is \(30\) cm more: \(4500 + 165 - 135 = 4530\). Correct average \(= 4530 \div 30 = 151\) cm.
Euler's formula: \(F + V - E = 2\), so \(40 + V - 60 = 2\) and \(V = 22\).
Two years of 5% growth multiplies the population by \(1.05^2 = 1.1025\). So the 2003 population \(= 66150 \div 1.1025 = 60000\). Check: \(60000 \to 63000 \to 66150\).

1 year 9 months \(= \frac{7}{4}\) years, so interest \(= P \times \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{7}{4} \div 100 = \frac{7P}{48}\). Amount \(= \frac{55P}{48} = 2475\), so \(P = ₹2160\). At 5% for 2 years, interest \(= 10\%\) of 2160 \(= 216\), amount \(= ₹2376\).

Look at the small triangle formed by the slanting line, the right side of the big triangle and the base. Its angle at the crossing point is e, and its angle on the base at the far right is \(180^\circ - g\) (g is the exterior angle there). Angle c is the exterior angle of this small triangle at the vertex on the base, so it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: \(c = e + (180^\circ - g)\).
LCM of 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 is \(120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5\). To make it a perfect square, each prime needs an even power: multiply by \(2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30\), giving \(3600 = 60^2\).
The smaller number is \(7^3 = 343\), so the larger is \(343 + 988 = 1331 = 11^3\). Its cube root is 11.
O(0, 0), A(0, 3), B(4, 3), C(4, 0) form a rectangle 4 units long and 3 units wide. Area \(= 4 \times 3 = 12\) square units.

\(4 \times 2\pi r h = 6 \times 2\pi r^2\) gives \(4h = 6r\), so \(r = \frac{2}{3} \times 12 = 8\) cm. Curved surface area \(= 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 8 \times 12 = \frac{4224}{7} \approx 603.43 \text{ cm}^2\).
Perimeter of the square \(= 240\) m, so the rectangle has \(2(80 + b) = 240\), \(b = 40\) m. Areas: square \(3600 \text{ m}^2\), rectangle \(3200 \text{ m}^2\). Difference \(= 400 \text{ m}^2\).

Units: \(A + A\) ends in 8, so A is 4 or 9. If \(A = 4\), the tens give \(4 + 4 = 8\), not 4. If \(A = 9\), units \(18\) (carry 1), tens \(9 + 9 + 1 = 19\) gives 9 (carry 1), hundreds \(2B + 1 = 3\) gives \(B = 1\). Check: \(199 + 199 = 398\).
\(5b9\) is divisible by 9, so \(5 + b + 9 = 14 + b\) is a multiple of 9, giving \(b = 4\). Then \(2a3 + 326 = 549\) gives \(2a3 = 223\), so \(a = 2\). \(b - a = 2\).

Seen from above, that is a row of three squares with one square above the middle square, which is figure (D).
Household expenditure takes \(144^\circ\) of the circle. \(\frac{144}{360} \times 72000 = 0.4 \times 72000 = ₹28800\).

I: subtraction is not commutative, e.g. \(3 - 1 = 2\) but \(1 - 3 = -2\). False. II: take \(x = 1, y = 2, z = 3\): \(1 + 6 = 7\) but \(3 \times 4 = 12\). Addition does not distribute over multiplication. False.
Shares are in the ratio of work done per day: \(\frac{1}{12} : \frac{1}{16} : \frac{1}{18} = 12 : 9 : 8\) (multiply by 144). A gets \(\frac{12}{29} \times 5800 = ₹2400\).

Circle: \(2\pi r = 88\) gives \(r = 14\) cm, area \(= \frac{22}{7} \times 196 = 616 \text{ cm}^2\). Square: side \(= 22\) cm, area \(= 484 \text{ cm}^2\). The circle encloses \(616 - 484 = 132 \text{ cm}^2\) more.
Circumference \(= 400 \times 66 = 26400\) cm \(= 264\) m. Diameter \(= 264 \times \frac{7}{22} = 84\) m.
For equal distances, average speed \(= \frac{2 \times 60 \times 90}{60 + 90} = \frac{10800}{150} = 72\) km/hr. Check with 180 km each way: 3 h + 2 h = 5 h for 360 km.
In order: 9.8, 10.6, 12.7, 13.4, 14.3, 15, 16.5, 17.2. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: \(\frac{13.4 + 14.3}{2} = 13.85\).

Measure directions from MQ. CD makes \(2x^\circ\) with CQ, and AB is parallel to CD, so AB also makes \(2x^\circ\) with that direction. MP makes \(100^\circ\) with MQ. The angle \(3x\) at A between AP and AB is therefore \(100 - 2x\). So \(3x = 100 - 2x\), giving \(x = 20\).

In triangle ABC, \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 51^\circ - 62^\circ = 67^\circ\). AE is parallel to BC, so \(\angle EAC = \angle ACB = 67^\circ\) (alternate angles). AEDF is a parallelogram (AE parallel to FD, AF parallel to ED), so adjacent angles add to \(180^\circ\): \(x = 180^\circ - 67^\circ = 113^\circ\).
The north and west walks are at right angles, so the diagonal is \(\sqrt{12^2 + 35^2} = \sqrt{144 + 1225} = \sqrt{1369} = 37\) m.
Take 200 adults and 300 children (500 people). Educated adults \(= 60\%\) of 200 \(= 120\); educated children \(= 85\%\) of 300 \(= 255\). Total educated \(= 375\), and \(\frac{375}{500} = 75\%\).

answers.value: B, E, C, A, D (Conscience, Consciousness, Consequence, Conservation, Consume)
answers.reasoning: All five start with CONS. Conscience and Consciousness have C as the 5th letter, which comes before E in Consequence and Conservation, and U in Consume. Conscie- comes before Consciou- (E before O). Conseq- comes before Conser- (Q before R). So the order is Conscience, Consciousness, Consequence, Conservation, Consume: B, E, C, A, D.
Each pair is two prime numbers in a row: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. Each pair starts with the second number of the pair before it, so after (11, 13) comes (13, 17).
Use letter positions. IFC is 9, 6, 3; NKH is 14, 11, 8; PMJ is 16, 13, 10: each steps back by 3. ROM is 18, 15, 13: it steps back by 3 and then by 2, so it is the odd one out.
The rule is cube the number and add 3: \(3^3 + 3 = 30\) and \(7^3 + 3 = 346\). So \(6^3 + 3 = 216 + 3 = 219\).
Each letter of RIGHT moves one place forward: R to S, I to J, G to H, H to I, T to U. Doing the same to FINDS gives F to G, I to J, N to O, D to E, S to T: GJOET.
We need the pattern N G K. It appears in "S N G K T" and in "U N G K X". Every other G has a different letter before or after it, so the count is 2.
In each figure, left number + top-right number - top-left number = right number. First figure: \(4 + 9 - 2 = 11\). Third figure: \(6 + 21 - 2 = 25\). So in the second figure \(P = 5 + 15 - 7 = 13\).

answers.reasoning: Count the lines in each arm. Figure 1 has one vertical and one horizontal line. Figure 2 doubles the vertical lines (two vertical, one horizontal). The last figure has three vertical and two horizontal lines, so the steps take turns: vertical goes up, then horizontal goes up, then vertical again. Each word's code is 3 times its number of letters: PEDESTRIAN has 10 letters (30), ACCIDENT 8 (24), DRIVER 6 (18). TRAFFIC has 7 letters, so its code is \(7 \times 3 = 21\).

3 erasers cost ₹ 9, so one eraser costs ₹ 3. Then 2 sharpeners + ₹ 6 = ₹ 14, so 2 sharpeners cost ₹ 8 and one costs ₹ 4. Finally 3 pencils + ₹ 4 = ₹ 25, so 3 pencils cost ₹ 21 and one pencil costs ₹ 7.

Mr. X can reach the rectangle in 3 ways: along the upper path, straight along the middle arrow, or along the lower path. From the rectangle there are 3 ways on to the home: round the top, round the bottom, or straight through along the dotted middle line. Each first choice can be followed by each second choice, so the number of ways is \(3 \times 3 = 9\).

Anita is older than Babita, who is older than Chetna. Chetna is older than Divya, and Erric is younger than Divya. So the order from oldest is Anita, Babita, Chetna, Divya, Erric, and the middle one is Chetna.
In each group the first number minus the second gives the third: \(99 - 25 = 74\), \(26 - 4 = 22\), \(45 - 9 = 36\). But \(64 - 14 = 50\), not 54, so [64, 14, 54] is different.

answers.value: Figure (1): top row down arrow, left arrow; bottom row right arrow, up arrow
answers.reasoning: From one figure to the next, each arrow stays in its corner and turns 90 degrees clockwise (up becomes right, right becomes down, down becomes left, left becomes up). Turning the second figure's arrows (right, down / up, left) gives down, left / right, up. Turning those again gives left, up / down, right, which is the last figure, so Figure (1) fits.

answers.reasoning: The mirror AB stands upright on the right, so left and right swap but top and bottom stay. The R and D boxes move to the left, R still on top and both letters reversed. Each number is the sum of the two before it: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 5 = 8, and so on. So the next number is 13 + 21 = 34.
The numbers 3, 6, 11, 18 go up by 3, 5, 7, so next is 18 + 9 = 27. The letters F, G, I, L move forward by 1, 2, 3, so next is L + 4 = P. The answer is 27P.
The largest 1-digit even number is 8, so the ones digit is 8 and the tens digit is 8 - 5 = 3. Since 758 - 354 = 404, the hundreds digit is 4. The thousands digit is 3 + 4 = 7, so the number is 7438.
A lake, a river and a pond are all bodies of water on the land. Rain is water falling from the sky, so it is the odd one out.
Add the letter positions: D = 4 and E = 5, so 4 + 5 = 9. In the same way F = 6 and G = 7, so 6 + 7 = 13.

answers.reasoning: First a person falls ill, then goes to a doctor, consults the doctor, receives treatment and finally recovers: Illness, Doctor, Consultation, Treatment, Recovery, which is C, A, D, E, B.

Small triangles: the top half has 3 pointing down and 2 pointing up, and the bottom half has 3 pointing up and 2 pointing down, which makes 10. Bigger triangles twice the height: 2 pointing down (each with its base on the top line) and 2 pointing up (each with its base on the bottom line), which makes 4 more. Total \(10 + 4 = 14\).

Count the letters as (c, b, a): cba is (1, 1, 1), cbaa is (1, 1, 2), cbbaa is (1, 2, 2). One letter is added each time, in the order a, b, c. So next is (2, 2, 2), which is ccbbaa, followed by ccbbaaa (2, 2, 3) and ccbbbaaa (2, 3, 3).
1st January falls on a Monday, so the 8th, 15th and 22nd are also Mondays. Counting on from the 22nd: 23rd Tuesday, 24th Wednesday, 25th Thursday.
Renaissance is spelt correctly. The others should be meagre (or meager), recommendation and irreparable.

answers.value: She is a mother and a teacher.
answers.reasoning: He becomes she and father becomes mother. Teacher is used for both men and women, so it does not change; "teacheress" is not a word.
"Was broken" is the simple past in the passive, so the active sentence also uses the simple past. "By whom" becomes the subject "Who": Who broke this beautiful glass?
"The ______ day of my life" compares this day with every other day, so it needs the superlative. Since nothing goes as planned, the day is bad, and the superlative of bad is worst.
To permit is to allow something to happen. To prevent is to stop it from happening, so prevent is the opposite. Allow and license mean much the same as permit.
"Though" pairs with "yet": Though she worked hard, yet she failed. "Although" would repeat "though", and "but" is not used after "though".
"Such a foolish decision" takes "a" because foolish begins with a consonant sound. "An impossible task" takes "an" because impossible begins with a vowel sound.
Bleak means dull, cheerless and without hope, which is what gloomy means. Balmy means pleasantly warm, and bemoan means to complain.
Escaping unhurt is a piece of good luck, so "Fortunately we escaped unhurt" makes sense. "Accidently" is also misspelt (the word is accidentally).

answers.value: I was annoyed at your behaviour.
answers.reasoning: The object "me" becomes the subject "I", and the past tense "annoyed" becomes "was annoyed". "Annoyed" is followed by "at" (or "by"), not "on", and "I were" is wrong, so the answer is "I was annoyed at your behaviour."

answers.runnerUp: B, if the setter treats "aloud" as meaning "loudly"
answers.reasoning: Loudly means with a lot of noise, which is what is not allowed in the park: We cannot play music loudly. "Aloud" is used with speaking or reading (read aloud) to mean "not silently", and "aloudly" is not a word.

answers.value: Pawan exclaimed that the scene was very beautiful.
answers.reasoning: An exclamation in reported speech uses "exclaimed that", turns "How beautiful" into "very beautiful", and changes "is" to "was" because the reporting verb is in the past. Only option D does all three.
When a question is reported with a question word like "what", we do not add "that". The correct sentence is "She asked me what had happened", so the error is in part (B).

answers.value: He said, "Mangal will be working hard."
answers.reasoning: In indirect speech "will" changes to "would". Going back to direct speech we change "would be working" back to "will be working": He said, "Mangal will be working hard."
The degrees are much/many (positive), more (comparative) and most (superlative). So the comparative that goes with "most" is "more".
A reed is a tall stem of grass you can write in the sand with, and to read is to look at writing and understand it. So: I wrote a line on the sand with a reed that she could not read.
"A dime a dozen" means very common and easy to find, which suits mediocre (ordinary) artists. "In rain or shine" means in all conditions, and "all and sundry" means everyone.
The sentence is positive and uses "we are", so the tag is negative and uses the same verb and subject: aren't we?

answers.value: Sunshine as well as snowstorm in short intervals
answers.reasoning: The passage says, "There may be sunshine one moment and a snowstorm the other." That sudden change is why the weather is called unpredictable.

answers.runnerUp: D, if the respect is read as coming from what mountaineers have learnt over time
answers.reasoning: The passage calls nature's glory "formidable" and lists the dangers on a mountain: storms, icy slopes, altitude sickness and frostbite. A mountaineer who does not respect these forces may not come back alive, so the respect comes from the need to survive.

answers.value: Opportunity to use sophisticated mountaineering equipment
answers.runnerUp: D, if the survival instinct is taken as having nothing to do with the joy of reaching the top
answers.reasoning: The passage says the joy comes from mastering something frightening, which is the feeling of achieving an impossible feat, and a summit also gives a grand view. Using fancy equipment is not mentioned and is not why climbers feel thrilled at the top, so it is the inappropriate reason.
Formidable means powerful and frightening to face. An opponent who beats someone in no time is a formidable one.
Arduous means needing a lot of effort and energy over a long time, as in the passage's "arduous journeys". Treacherous means dangerous, and exhaustion and endeavour are nouns.

answers.value: DBCA: The performance of our players was rather worse than I expected.
answers.reasoning: The subject is "The performance of our players" (D, B), followed by the verb part "was rather worse" (C) and then the comparison "than I expected" (A). So the order is DBCA.

answers.runnerUp: C, if abandon is taken in the sense of giving up an activity, whose opposite is to continue
answers.reasoning: To abandon something is to give it up or leave it behind, as in abandoning an idea or a pet. To adopt is to take something up and make it your own, so it is the opposite. Chastise means to scold and solicit means to ask for, so they do not fit.

answers.reasoning: The Moon is a satellite of the Earth, Cassiopeia is a constellation, Halley is a comet and Sirius is a star. So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. The remaining 1% is argon, carbon dioxide and other gases.
Methane, carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide are the natural greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. Ethane is not counted among them.

Tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium, Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes, malaria is caused by a protozoan (Plasmodium) and AIDS is caused by a virus (HIV). So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
Microorganisms are grouped into four major groups: bacteria, fungi, protozoa and algae. Viruses are studied separately, and the other options mix in single organisms or substances.
Adrenalin is released by the adrenal glands when we are angry, worried or embarrassed. It raises the heart rate and breathing so the body can cope with the stress.
Making compost with the help of red worms is called vermicomposting. The worms eat the waste and turn it into rich manure.

Biodiversity is the variety of organisms on the earth, their relationships with one another and with the environment. The biosphere is the part of the earth where life exists, which is a different idea.
Satpura National Park in Madhya Pradesh (the Bori forest) is the first Reserve Forest of India. Tawa is a reservoir, not a forest.

answers.value: Increased activity of sweat glands and sebaceous glands
answers.runnerUp: B, if the question wants only the gland that actually causes acne (oil glands), rather than the textbook's wording
answers.reasoning: During adolescence the sweat glands and the sebaceous (oil) glands become more active. The textbook says that acne and pimples appear because of the increased activity of these glands in the skin, so both are named.
Earthquake tremors are caused by a disturbance deep inside the earth's crust, where the plates of the crust move against each other.
The heat energy produced by the complete combustion of 1 kg of a fuel is called its calorific value, measured in kJ/kg.
Gold is used for jewellery, iron for machinery, mercury in thermometers and copper for electric wires. So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.
A magnet can pull or push another magnet or a piece of iron without touching it, so magnetic force is a non-contact force.
Kharif crops are sown in the rainy season (June to September): paddy, cotton and soyabean are kharif crops. Mustard is sown in winter, so it is a rabi crop.

answers.value: Shaking hands with an infected person
answers.reasoning: HIV spreads through body fluids: from an infected mother through her milk, through shared syringes and through sexual contact. It does not spread by shaking hands or other casual touch.
Natural gas is mostly methane, and CNG is natural gas stored under high pressure. So the major component of CNG is methane.
Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen and gives off heat (and often light).
Animal cells have a nucleus, cell membrane and cytoplasm. The cell wall is found only in plant cells (and in bacteria and fungi), not in animal cells.
Animals that give birth to young ones, like humans, cows and dogs, are called viviparous. Animals that lay eggs are oviparous.
Aeroplanes, boats and fish have streamlined shapes so that the drag (fluid friction) on them is as small as possible.
Using horns less, planting trees along roads and fitting silencers to aircraft engines all reduce noise. Cutting trees around houses removes a barrier to sound and increases noise, so (D) is wrong.

answers.value: Virtual, behind the mirror and the same size as the object
answers.reasoning: A plane mirror forms an image that cannot be caught on a screen (virtual), appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and is the same size as the object.

Sodium reacts so vigorously with water that it catches fire, which is why it is stored in kerosene. Zinc and cobalt react only slowly, and phosphorus does not react with water (it is stored under water).

When current passes through a conducting solution, bubbles of gas may form on the electrodes, metal may be deposited on an electrode, and the colour of the solution may change. So (A), (B) and (D) are correct and (C) is wrong.
A Municipal Corporation collects garbage, prevents the outbreak of diseases and runs schools. Defence is the work of the Union government, not of a city body.
The Sahara desert covers a large part of northern Africa.
The factors of soil formation are parent rock, climate, relief, flora, fauna and micro-organisms, and time. Precipitation is not listed as a separate factor; it is part of climate.
Jute is called the golden fibre because of its golden shine and its value as a cash crop.
In 1930 Gandhiji walked from Sabarmati to Dandi and made salt from sea water to break the British salt law, which gave the government a monopoly on salt.
Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor. After the revolt of 1857 the British exiled him to Rangoon. The others were leaders of the 1857 revolt or a nawab of Awadh.
Marine based industries use products from the sea, such as fish and other sea food. Cotton textile is agro based and pharmaceuticals are chemical industries.
Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability. Article 14 is equality before law, Article 19 is freedom of speech and Article 21 is the right to life.
Australia is the largest producer of bauxite, the ore of aluminium, in the world.

In Mughal administration the diwan was the financial officer, the bakhshi was the military paymaster, the faujdar was the military commander of a district and the kotwal was the town police commander.

answers.value: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
answers.reasoning: CITES (printed here as CITIES) stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, an international agreement that controls trade in endangered animals and plants.
The Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act was passed in 1993.
The natural growth rate of population is the birth rate minus the death rate.
Solar energy is renewed all the time by the sun. Petroleum, natural gas and coal take millions of years to form, so they are non-renewable.
Amar Jiban, published in 1876, was written by Rashsundari Devi, a housewife in Bengal who secretly learnt to read. It is the first full autobiography in the Bengali language.
PIL stands for Public Interest Litigation, which lets any person or group go to the High Court or Supreme Court on behalf of those whose rights are violated.
Subhas Chandra Bose led the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) to free India from British rule during the Second World War.
Ibn Battuta was a fourteenth century traveller from Morocco in Africa who visited India during the rule of Muhammad bin Tughluq.
The government has three organs: the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
Planting trees (afforestation) holds the soil together and conserves land. Overgrazing, chemical pesticides and land degradation all harm land.

answers.value: Buying and selling takes place between traders
answers.reasoning: A shopping complex has branded stores, many products under one roof and often entertainment. Buying and selling between traders happens in a wholesale market, not a shopping complex.
The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale.
The power of the courts to strike down a law passed by Parliament that goes against the basic structure of the Constitution is called judicial review.

answers.value: The ward Panchs and the Sarpanch form the Gram Sabha.
answers.reasoning: The ward Panchs and the Sarpanch form the Gram Panchayat, not the Gram Sabha. The Gram Sabha is made of all adults (18 years or more) living in the Panchayat area, and it checks and approves the Panchayat's work.

Public facilities such as water, health and sanitation meet people's basic needs (A is correct), and providing them is the government's responsibility (C is correct). They are meant for everyone, not only those who can pay (B is wrong), and private companies run for profit, so (D) is wrong.
